summary: Milestone 2026.10.721 completed 8 experiments (1 compute-bound, 7 synthesis-only) across 51.2 total wall-time minutes (averaging 6 minutes per experiment) reconstructed from disk-mtime fallback data. Execution wall time was led by two synthesis-only tasks—reconciling fourteen outcomes and deciding utility and deployment continuation (11.19 minutes) and qualifying two missed utility-audit rejection branches (10.87 minutes)—alongside the sole compute-bound task qualifying typed runtime references without treating annotation prose as paths (8.88 minutes), with table interpolation error bounding (6.21 minutes) and hardware transaction mapping (5.79 minutes) rounding out the top five. With gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks recorded as false, the point-in-time monitor reading of 0% GPU utilization (2MB allocated) on the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 reflects expected post-run idle state for non-GPU synthesis workloads, and single-model compute execution correctly avoided multi-model DualGPURunner dispatch.
bottlenecks_identified: Synthesis-only tasks accounted for 7 of 8 completed experiments and four of the top five slowest runs totaling 34.06 minutes out of 51.2 total wall-time minutes, led by fourteen-outcome reconciliation (11.19 minutes) and utility-audit rejection branch qualification (10.87 minutes).

The sole compute-bound task ('Qualify typed runtime references without treating annotation prose as paths') required 8.88 minutes, but existing experiment receipts lack intra-task phase breakdown (environment preflight, model execution, artifact serialization) to pinpoint internal execution latency.

Long-running synthesis tasks (outcome reconciliation, audit branch qualification, table interpolation error bounding, and hardware operation mapping) executed serially without incremental receipt caching or evidence memoization when upstream inputs were unchanged.
